steps: Check codes & permits
Install to CAN/CSA-B365 and local rules; local building officials approve the installation. Do not install in any fireplace or connect to an air distribution duct or system.

Install to CAN/CSA-B365, Installation Code for Solid-Fuel-Burning Appliances and Equipment, and get all necessary approvals from the local building officials, who have final authority.

  • Plan so the stove and chimney connector meet all clearance requirements.
  • Plan floor protection that is adequate and made to the requirements.
  • Do not install in any fireplace. Do not connect to any air distribution duct or system.

The data plate on the back of the stove gives the safety testing information, the certified testing laboratory and the installation requirements.
Unpack & check loose parts
Check the fire bricks are firmly in place, the air control works freely and the baffles sit correctly. The glove and ceramic flue connection gasket are usually in the ashpan or firebox.
Chimney / flue system
Code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner or listed type HT factory-built; min. 6" internal; one flue per appliance; flue supported independently of the stove.

• USA: High Temperature (H.T.) chimney to UL-103-1985 (2100º F.) or code-approved masonry with flue liner. Canada: High Temperature (650ºC) to ULC S-629.
  • Chimney and connector internal size not less than 6 inches diameter, and not significantly larger: too large a section cools the flue gases, causing sluggish or unpredictable performance.
  • Do not connect to a flue serving any other appliance.
  • Recommended (not required): at least 16 feet of chimney above the stove, flue collar to chimney top.

Roof construction, large trees nearby and high altitude can affect draft; consult a local professional chimney sweep or the Morsø dealer. The manual shows typical factory-built and masonry chimney installations as a drawing on this page.
Set top or rear flue exit
The stove ships with a round blanking plate. For a rear exit, knock out the round panel on the rear heat shield plate, swap the blanking plate and flue collar, push down and tighten the screws.
Run the chimney connector
Required between stove and chimney: 6" (150mm), 24 MSG black or blue single-wall or listed double-wall, never galvanized; three screws at every joint; seal airtight.

Diameter6 inches (150mm)
Single-wall24 gauge or heavier steel, no galvanized
Double-walltested and listed for solid fuel
Horizontal run3 feet (1 metre) recommended max
Total lengthno longer than 8 feet (2.5 metres)
Slopeup 1/4 inch per foot (20 mm per metre) toward the chimney
Turnsno more than two 90 degree
Horizontal run to ceiling18 inches

Do not install the chimney directly at the stove outlet. Secure the connector with a minimum of three screws to the stove and to each adjoining section. Use mild bends (45º rather than 90º) and keep every part accessible for cleaning. Do not pass the connector through an attic, closet or similar concealed space; avoid combustible walls and ceilings where possible, and make any combustible wall pass-through to CAN/CSA-B365.

The manual refers to a section on wall pass-throughs that is not in its text; check the PDF. Wear gloves and protective eyewear when drilling, cutting or joining connector sections.
Position for clearances
Place the stove to the clearance chart for your layout and connector (standard single- or double-wall, rear vent, alcove), then connect the flue. Keep 30" to furniture.

• Standard installation, single- or double-wall connector: chart on this page.
  • Rear vent out the back wall (single-wall) and alcove (double-wall): charts on p. 9.
  • Next to non-combustible materials a gap of 4 inches or more is recommended, for cleaning and so heat circulates into the room.
  • Recommended minimum to furniture: 30 inches.

See the clearance cards for the values.
Floor protection
Non-combustible pad beneath the stove extending 16" to the front and 6" to the sides (US); with a rear exit, also under the connector and 2" beyond each side.
Mobile home (USA only)
Outside combustion air kit, stove bolted through the hearth pad, listed Type HT connector and chimney with a spark-arrestor cap; install per 24 CFR, Part 3280 (HUD). Not permitted in Canada.
Fresh air supply

Unless air leaks in enough naturally, fit a dedicated inlet with 2 square inches (1250 square mm) of free air space; not on a wall subject to negative wind pressure, not directly across from the stove.
First fire
Make sure the baffles are placed correctly. Keep the first fire small so the paint cures and the main plates settle; ventilate the room against paint fumes.

panels.title: Smoke or a sluggish fire
items: Smoke or fumes when lighting or reloading, or a fire that won't respond → poor draft (rarely, too little fresh air into the room)
Suddenly sluggish → soot fall around the flue collar or in the flue/chimney
Sluggish or unpredictable → flue section too large, flue gases cool too much
Back-puffing and sluggishness → overly dry wood that is gray in color

panels.title: Over-firing
items: Any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows
Flue temperature above 450° C (750°F), measured 20 cm above the stove
Baffle distorted by an overfire → replace it as soon as possible
Fast internal wear → persistent heavy firing, soot and ashes left to accumulate

panels.title: Dirty or misting glass
items: Fuel too wet: wood spits or sizzles and the glass persistently mists up
Logs too large or not split
Combustion temperatures too low, or the stove run too slowly

panels.title: Fire hard to control
items: Door gasket hardened: door difficult to close or air leaking in → replace the gasket
New load won't light → leave the door slightly ajar until it kindles
Logs not alight within 2 minutes → in an extreme case the flue gases can ignite; have a good layer of embers before refilling

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
A cold stove needs plenty of air to get going. Morsø recommends the top-down method: it's the cleanest way to light, and it keeps soot off the glass.

  1. Build the fire with two firelighters and about 2-4 lbs of dry kindling sticks. Put the firelighters directly under the top layer of kindling.
  2. Open the air fully: move the air lever above the door all the way to the right.
  3. Light the fire.
  4. Partly close the door, leaving it open an inch or two so plenty of air gets in. Don't leave the stove while the door is open.
  5. After about 5-10 minutes, when the chimney is warm, close the door. A good layer of embers forms after about 15-20 minutes.
Your very first fire: keep it small, so the paint can cure and the main plates can settle into position. The paint gives off some fumes, so ventilate the room.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire. Keep them away from the stove while it's in use.

reload.title: Reloading and the air lever
reload.html:
The air lever

The lever above the door controls the main (primary) air. Move it right to open it; preheated air then enters through the airwash system above the glass. All the way left is the lowest burn rate. A second (secondary) air supply feeds the flames above the fire. It is always open and can't be adjusted.

Adding wood

  1. Reload while there are still plenty of live embers. Use a poker to spread them across the firebox floor, with plenty toward the front.
  2. Lay two pieces of wood on the embers, half an inch or more apart.
  3. Close the door and leave the air fully open. If the wood doesn't catch, leave the door slightly ajar until it does, then close it.
  4. After a few minutes, set the air lever for the heat you want. Always leave enough air for clear, lasting flames.

Keep the wood below the stainless-steel air box on the back wall of the firebox. The space in front of and above it is kept free for burning the gases from the wood.

Less heat: less wood, less air. More heat: more wood, more air. Before you turn the lever fully left, burn at a medium rate (lever mid-range) for about 15 minutes.
Note: p. 15 recommends a fuel load of 3 lbs (2 pieces) up to 6 lbs (5 pieces); p. 28 says to refuel with 2 - 3 pieces of wood, no more than 2 - 2.5 kg.

wood.title: Choosing and storing wood
wood.html:
The stove is listed for burning wood only. Burn natural wood that is well seasoned and dry.

Lengthmax 12 inches (30 cm)
Maker's website: Log Size 11".
Moistureno more than 20%

Split the wood so it dries, then stack it under cover where air can move around each piece. Some softwoods are ready after one good summer; oak, maple and elm may need up to 18 months. The Morsø Moisture Meter (part # 62929900) checks it for you.

Is it dry enough?

Seasoned wood feels light and shows cracks running out from the center at the ends. If it spits or sizzles and the glass keeps misting up, it's too wet. Avoid very dry, gray wood too: it can cause back-puffing and a sluggish fire.

Never burn

Garbage, lawn clippings or yard waste, anything containing rubber (tires included) or plastic, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products, anything containing asbestos, construction or demolition debris, railroad ties, pressure-treated wood, manure or animal remains, salt-water driftwood or anything else previously saturated with salt water, unseasoned wood, or paper products, cardboard, plywood and particleboard. Burning these may release toxic fumes, or make the stove ineffective and cause smoke. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Note: p. 12 says to split the wood to approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section; p. 28 says the wood should be split and 8 - 12 cm thick.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
When you run the stove at the right temperatures, the glass stays mostly clean. Dirt that settles while you light it usually burns off as the stove heats up.

For heavier deposits

  • Wait until the glass is cold. Never clean it hot.
  • Use Morsø glass cleaner and follow its instructions.
  • Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass.

Why the glass gets dirty

  • The wood is too wet or not well seasoned.
  • The logs are too large or not split.
  • The fire burns too cool, for example when the stove is run too slowly.
Cracked or broken glass: don't use the stove until it's replaced, and use only Morsø high-temperature ceramic glass from your dealer. To avoid breaking it, don't strike the glass or slam the door.

Old ceramic glass can't go in ordinary glass recycling. Hand it in at a recycling station as ceramic glass.

overfire.title: Over-firing: burning too hot
overfire.html:
Do not over-fire the stove. Over-firing means burning it too hot. It can cause a house fire or permanently damage the stove.

  • If any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows, you are over-firing.
  • Don't overload the firebox. The load limits are under "Reload & set the air".
  • Never try to get more heat by changing the air control's range. The minimum burn rate is set at the factory, and altering it is against federal regulations.

Flue temperature

Normal (approx.)300° C (550°F)
Never above450° C (750°F)

This is measured on the stove pipe about 20 cm (8") above the stove. The Morsø Flue Gas Thermometer (part # 62901200) attaches there with a magnet.

Note: p. 16 gives the flue temperature limit as 450° C (750°F) and the normal flue temperature as approx. 300° C (550°F); in both pairs the Celsius and Fahrenheit figures printed together are not the same temperature.

If the baffle warps after an over-fire, the stove still works but may be less efficient. Replace it as soon as possible.

ash.title: Emptying the ash
ash.html:
Empty the ash pan daily or as needed. Ash that builds up toward the underside of the grate traps heat and can make the grate fail early. If you can, leave a 1-1.5 inch (2-3 cm) layer of ash on the firebox floor; it insulates the fire.

  1. Open the front door. Use a shovel or poker to stir the extra ash through the slots in the grate into the ash pan.
  2. Lift out the ash pan, keeping it level so ash doesn't spill.
  3. Tip the ash into a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  4. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  5. Put the ash pan back and close the door.

If you'll bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled.

Never empty the stove while it's burning, and never use a household or shop vacuum to remove ash.

chimney.title: Chimney care and creosote
chimney.html:
Slow fires give off tar and vapors that condense in the cool chimney as creosote. If creosote catches fire, it burns extremely hot, so keep the chimney clean.

  • At least every two months in the heating season, inspect the chimney and the chimney connector (the pipe from the stove to the chimney) for creosote, and remove any build-up.
  • About monthly at first, check for soot above the baffle plate and around the flue outlet.
  • After each season, clean the flue all the way from the stove to the top. Before the season, check for bird's nests or other blockages.
  • Suddenly sluggish? Check for soot that has fallen around the flue collar or in the chimney.

To look inside, let the stove cool completely, then use a mirror to sight up through the flue collar. If you can't inspect or clean it yourself, call your Morsø dealer or a professional chimney sweep.

Chimney fire? Act fast: close the air control, get everyone out of the house, and call the fire department.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's burning. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn your skin.
  • Run it only with the door fully closed. Never leave it unattended with the door open: smoke and flames can be drawn out into the room.
  • Keep furniture at least 30 inches away, and the same for drying clothes, newspapers, firewood and other things that can burn.
  • Build the fire directly on the hearth. Don't raise it on a grate, andirons or anything else.
  • Don't alter the stove. Changes can cause a fire or carbon monoxide poisoning, and they void the warranty.

Detectors

Morsø recommends a smoke detector in the room where the stove is. Also put at least one smoke detector on each floor, away from the stove and close to where people sleep; one too close to the stove may go off when a puff of smoke escapes while you reload. Some areas require smoke and carbon monoxide detectors where heaters are installed.

When you clean or service the stove, wear safety goggles and gloves.

care.title: Yearly care and the off-season
care.html:
Before each heating season

  • Clean the chimney and chimney connector thoroughly, and replace or repair damaged sections.
  • Check the gaskets for wear or flattening, and replace them if needed.
  • Check the glass for cracks.
  • Check that the door and handle are tight, and adjust them if needed.

Door gasket: the rope seal around the door can harden over time. Replace it if the door gets hard to close, or if air leaks in around it and the fire gets harder to control. Your stove supplier has a Morsø rope gasket kit.

Inside parts such as the bricks, baffles and grate wear from the heat. Replace damaged parts soon, with original Morsø parts.

Outside: vacuum with a soft brush or wipe with a lint-free cloth. If the paint turns slightly gray, Morsø touch-up spray paint is available from your supplier. Expect a slight smell the next time you light the stove, and ventilate the room.

Off-season

Clean the stove out thoroughly, because leftover ash soaks up moisture and causes rust. Leave the air control slightly open. Fit a chimney cap so rain can't reach the stove, but don't block the flue completely. A desiccant such as kitty litter in the ash pan absorbs summer moisture; remove it before the heating season.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
If an authorised Morsø dealer supplied your stove, Morsø's limited warranty runs for 10 years from the date of purchase. It covers repair or replacement of parts that are defective in material or workmanship, including manufacturing defects in the main exterior body parts.

Not covered

  • Wear parts: smoke deflector plates, grates, refractory stones/plates, glass and sealing materials, plus normal wear such as discoloration.
  • Damage from improper installation or use, overheating, or the wrong fuel.
  • Repairs or modifications Morsø didn't authorize.
  • Corrosion after a lack of maintenance or damage to the surface finish.
  • Problems caused by local conditions, draft problems or a damaged or faulty chimney.
Voids the warranty: not installing, running and maintaining the stove as the manual says; burning materials it isn't EPA-certified for; unauthorized modifications.

To make a claim

Contact Morsø Customer Service at info@morsoe.com or +45 96691900. Have your proof of purchase, the model and serial number, and a description of the problem (with photos if you can).

specFlue.html:

No galvanized connector. Minimum of three screws to the stove and to each adjoining section; seal every joint so the system is airtight to the chimney outlet. Keep horizontal runs 18 inches from the ceiling.

Top or rear outlet: the stove ships with a round blanking plate. For the rear, knock out the round panel on the rear heat shield plate to reveal the cast iron plate, untwist the blanking plate and the flue collar and swap them, then push down and tighten the enclosed screws.

specClear.title: Clearances · standard installation
specClear.html:

B · Backwall to unit3" (76 mm) / 2" (51 mm)
C · Cornerwall to unit5" (127 mm) / 5" (127 mm)

Rear vent out back wall, single-wall connector (p. 9): sidewall to unit 10" (254 mm), backwall to unit 6.5" (165 mm), sidewall to connector 15.5" (394 mm); no other values given.

Increase distances for heat-sensitive materials. Next to non-combustible materials, 4 inches or more is recommended. Furniture: 30 inches recommended minimum.

Note: on the minimum distance to combustibles, the text on p. 8 says never to install the stove within 8 inches of combustible materials around the sides or 16 inches above the top; the clearance charts on pp. 8-9 list backwall-to-unit 2" to 6.5" and cornerwall-to-unit 5".
Note: p. 4 says do not install the stove in any fireplace; p. 8 says fireplace installations require greater clearances above the stove and points to the clearance chart, which has no fireplace entry.

specAlcove.html:

The chart gives no cornerwall values (C, F) for an alcove and lists only a double-wall connector. The floor protector must be non-combustible and extend beneath the heater and to the front, sides and rear; see the floor protection card. The manual's alcove drawing on this page shows where the lettered distances are measured.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
The heater meets CAN/ULC-S627 for a combustible floor and needs no radiant floor protection. It does need a non-combustible pad against falling embers.

Front16" US · 450 mm Canada
Right / left side6" US · 200 mm Canada
Backnone listed US · 200 mm Canada

US: beneath the heater and 16" to the front and 6" to the sides of the fuel loading door and ash removal openings. With a rear exit, also beneath the chimney connector and 2 inches beyond each side (p. 8).

Canada (CSA B365): continuous, durable non-combustible ember pad beneath the appliance, at least 450 mm (18 in) beyond any side with a door, across the full width plus 200 mm (8 in) each side, and 200 mm (8 in) on other sides. Less than 200 mm (8 in) from a wall, the pad need only reach the base of the wall. Not on carpet unless structurally supported.

specMobile.title: Mobile home installation
specMobile.html:
USA only. In Canada, do not install in a transportable building or mobile home.

  • Outside combustion air kit, installed per the kit's guide. Intake piping can run through the floor into a vented crawl space or through the wall to outside air.
  • Secure the stove by bolting through the hearth pad into the flooring.
  • Listed Type HT chimney connector and HT chimney, terminal cap with spark arrestor. Never a single-wall connector (stovepipe).
  • Floor protection exactly per section 1.5.
  • Top chimney sections removable, for a maximum clearance of 13.5' from ground level in transport.
  • Install per 24 CFR, Part 3280 (HUD) and the chimney and connector makers' instructions.
Never draw combustion air from a wall, floor or ceiling cavity or from an enclosed space such as an attic or garage. Do not install in a sleeping room. Do not cut floor joists, wall studs or ceiling trusses.

The parts list includes a bracket for the optional outside air kit (SKU 71613700, p. 25).

conflicts.issue: Fuel load size: 3 lbs (2 pieces) up to 6 lbs (5 pieces) on p. 15 and a 6lbs (5 split logs) maximum on p. 16, vs. 2 - 3 pieces, no more than 2 - 2.5 kg on the p. 28 quick guide. Also flagged in specFuel.
Split size: approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section on p. 12 vs. 8 - 12 cm thick on p. 28. Also flagged in specFuel.
Flue temperatures printed as 450° C (750°F) maximum and approx. 300° C (550°F) normal; the Celsius and Fahrenheit figures are not equivalent, so the limit differs depending on which unit is read.
Text says never within 8 inches of combustible materials around the sides; the clearance charts list backwall-to-unit 3"/2" (standard), 6.5" (rear vent), 3" (alcove) and cornerwall-to-unit 5".
p. 4 says do not install in any fireplace; p. 8 says fireplace installations require greater clearances above the stove (see the clearance chart), but the chart has no fireplace entry.

review.notes: The manual covers the whole Morsø 6100 B series; the 6140 B is named only on the parts diagram (p. 23), and 'low base' appears nowhere, so nothing in the guide is specific to the low base. The catalog feature 'Takes logs up to 11 in' carries the same log-length mismatch as log_length_max_in. The manual gives no firebox volume, dimensions, weight, heating area, burn times or blower, so those are left out; catalog heat output, efficiency, emissions, EPA 2020, non-catalytic, 6 in flue (top or rear), outside air and US mobile-home approval all match. p. 7 has no extractable text, and the 'Wall Pass-Throughs' section that p. 6 refers to is not in the text; the guide points to the PDF. Chimney installations (p. 5) and the lettered clearance/floor-protection drawings (pp. 8-9) are figures; values were taken only from the text tables. The manual says not to use a grate to elevate the fire (pp. 11-12) yet refers to the stove's grate and its ash slots (pp. 18-19); the parts list shows no grate. Both are repeated as written. The mobile-home list (p. 11) includes a Canadian chimney requirement (6" (152 mm) factory-built, CAN/ULC-629M) although it says not to install in Canadian mobile homes; left out of the guide. Smoke detectors: p. 16 recommends one in the stove's room and one per floor away from the appliance near sleeping areas; both are given. Kindling 2-4 lbs (p. 14) vs 1 - 2 kg (p. 28) and the fresh-air inlet 2 square inches (1250 square mm) are approximate equivalents; shown as printed, not flagged. 'kitter litter' (p. 22) is rendered as kitty litter. The parts list (pp. 24-25) has repeated or inconsistent SKUs (e.g. 731640 for both M6x55 and M6x40 screws); only the outside-air bracket SKU is used.
